documents.title: Lease contract
documents.why: The landlord's duty is measured by the designated use; the lease records the rented dwelling and its agreed use.

must_show: the defect and where it is
how the use of the dwelling is affected
documents.title: Record of the defect (dated photographs, inspection or expert report)
documents.why: The tenant's rights arise where a defect arises or the agreed use is disturbed; dated photographs or an inspection report ordinarily prove that the defect exists, where it is and since when.

must_show: how and when the landlord learned of the defect
documents.title: Proof of when the landlord learned of the defect (tenant's dated notice, landlord's or manager's acknowledgement, or inspection record)
documents.why: The remedies depend on the landlord being aware of the defect, and a reduction runs from the time he became aware (art. 259d); a dated written notice, a written acknowledgement or an inspection record ordinarily proves when that was. Where the claim states that the landlord was told only orally, no such record exists and none is requested.

documents.title: Proof of the damage (invoices, receipts, photographs of damaged items)
documents.why: Liability covers damage the defect caused; invoices, receipts and photographs of damaged items ordinarily prove the damage and its amount.

must_show: announcement that rent will be deposited
documents.title: Tenant's written time limit to the landlord and written announcement of the deposit
documents.why: The time limit (and the announcement of the deposit) must be in writing, so the tenant's letter itself is the proof that they were given and when.

must_show: due date of the first deposited rent
the date on which the claims were brought before the conciliation authority, or a sentence that they have not yet been brought
documents.title: Receipt of the deposit office for the deposited rent and the tenant's application to the conciliation authority
documents.why: The deposited rent passes to the landlord unless claims are brought before the conciliation authority within 30 days of the due date of the first deposited rent; the deposit office's receipt shows that due date and the application shows whether and when the claims were brought.

facts.question: Which tenancy dispute does the claim concern: a defect of the dwelling or a disturbance of its agreed use that the tenant did not cause (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails), a termination of the lease by the landlord, or a rent increase? A rent increase that the landlord accompanied with a notice of termination is a rent increase dispute: the rent-increase rules examine that notice (art. 269d para. 2 let. c).

Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?
Does the claim state that the landlord does not yet know of the defect (the tenant has not reported it and the landlord has not learned of it in another way)?
Does the claim state that the landlord learned of the defect only orally, so that no written notice, written acknowledgement or inspection record of it exists?
Does the tenant claim compensation from the landlord for damage the defect caused to the tenant (for example damaged furniture or clothing, or extra costs)?
Does the claim state that the tenant intends to pay the rent on deposit with the office designated by the canton instead of to the landlord, or has begun to do so?
Does the claim state that at least one rent payment has already been paid into deposit with the office designated by the canton?

notes.text: Convention of this benchmark (not law): A fact that the file does not mention is taken as not alleged, and the rules are applied as if it were absent. Silence never ends a process: where a fact's absence would end it, the unmentioned fact is unresolved. The defining event is never presumed: if the file does not mention it, it is unresolved. A fact that the file raises and leaves unsettled is open. The defining event (defect_present) and any always-stated fact carry no presumption.

Is a rent deposit intended or made?
